sql:
SELECT z.Borough, COUNT(*) AS touches
FROM lake.trips t
JOIN ops.zones z ON z.LocationID = t.PULocationID OR z.LocationID = t.DOLocationID
GROUP BY z.Borough
ORDER BY z.Borough

diagnosis.bottleneck: The OR join condition (z.LocationID = t.PULocationID OR z.LocationID = t.DOLocationID) forces a blockwise nested loop join between 495K trips rows and 265 zones rows instead of a hash join, causing ~495K * 265 key comparisons with two equality checks per row.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: INNER | Condition: ((LocationID = CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT)) OR (LocationID = CAST(DOLocationID AS BIGINT)

hypotheses.claim: An OR inside the JOIN condition cannot use a hash join; the engine falls back to a nested-loop style join, which is far more expensive than two equi-joins. (matched: inner join ops.zones z on z.locationid = t.pulocationid or z.locationid = t.dolocationid)

The BLOCKWISE_NL_JOIN is chosen because the OR predicate prevents hash join optimization; rewriting as a UNION ALL of two separate joins (one on PULocationID, one on DOLocationID) would enable hash joins and avoid the nested loop.

The CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) and CAST(DOLocationID AS BIGINT) suggest possible type mismatch; ensuring LocationID, PULocationID, and DOLocationID share the same integer type could eliminate casts and improve predicate evaluation speed.
The HASH_GROUP_BY operates on the join output which may duplicate trips rows matching both PU and DO zones; pre-aggregating trips by location before joining could reduce rows entering the join.
